summary.title: x86 Options (Using the GNU Compiler Collection (GCC))
summary.one_liner: Learn what GCC's -march and -mtune x86 flags do, and which cpu-type values (from i386 up to x86-64-v4, Intel, AMD and VIA chips) select which instruction sets.
keywords: gcc target cpu for intel and amd
takeaways: -march=cpu-type lets GCC emit instructions that may not run on other processors, while -mtune only adjusts scheduling and tuning for that CPU.
-march=native enables every instruction subset supported by the local machine, so the resulting binary may not run elsewhere.
The x86-64-v2, v3 and v4 values select psABI micro-architecture levels and use generic tuning, unless you add an explicit -mtune.
The page lists every accepted cpu-type, from i386 and Pentium variants through Intel Core, Atom and AMD K8/Zen families to VIA and ZHAOXIN, with the instruction set extensions each one enables.
summary.summary: This GCC manual section documents the x86-specific -m options, focusing on -march=cpu-type and its counterpart -mtune=cpu-type. It explains that -march permits code that may fail on other processors, while -mtune only tunes scheduling for a given chip. The page then enumerates every accepted cpu-type value, listing for each the instruction set extensions (MMX, SSE through AVX-512, AMX and so on) it supports, grouped by Intel, AMD, and VIA/ZHAOXIN families. The listing is a reference table rather than a tutorial, and the -mprefer-vector-width option mentioned in the listing is not covered in the text provided.
technologies: x86 SIMD (MMX, SSE, AVX, AVX2, AVX-512)
